How this book matches your exam. Research check: this book follows NCERT Class 11 Chemistry Part 1, Unit 1 (Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry), for the CBSE 2026–27 session. In the rationalised syllabus, the Class 11 theory paper is 70 marks, 3 hours, plus 30 practical marks, across nine units; Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry carries about 7 marks. The unit covers the importance of chemistry, nature of matter, laws of chemical combination, Dalton's atomic theory, atoms, molecules and elements, atomic and molecular masses, the mole concept and molar mass, percentage composition, empirical and molecular formulae, chemical reactions, stoichiometry and calculations based on it, and concentration terms.

Each unit ends with a 10-mark practice set. Atomic masses: H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, Na = 23, S = 32, Cl = 35.5, Ca = 40 (H = 1.008 where stated). N_A = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹. Every numerical answer was checked by computer. The marking points are our own, not the official CBSE marking scheme.

Unit 1 of 10: Matter, Measurement and Significant Figures

Key ideas

  • Matter: anything with mass that occupies space; states — solid, liquid, gas. Classification: pure substances (elements, compounds) and mixtures (homogeneous, heterogeneous).
  • SI units: mass (kg), length (m), time (s), temperature (K), amount (mol). Volume: 1 L = 1 dm³ = 1000 cm³.
  • Scientific notation: N × 10ⁿ (1 ≤ N < 10).
  • Significant figures: non-zero digits count; zeros between them count; leading zeros don't; trailing zeros after a decimal point count. Multiply/divide → fewest significant figures; add/subtract → fewest decimal places.
  • Accuracy (closeness to true value) vs precision (closeness of repeated values).

Worked examples

Example 1: How many significant figures in 0.0025 and 2.500? Answer: 2 and 4.

10-mark practice set

  1. (1 mark, MCQ) Which is a homogeneous mixture? (a) sand and water (b) air (c) oil and water (d) iron filings and sulphur. Answer: (b).
  2. (1 mark) Express 0.000345 in scientific notation. Answer: 3.45 × 10⁻⁴.
  3. (2 marks) Calculate 2.5 × 1.25 with the correct number of significant figures. Answer: 3.125 (1); rounded to 2 s.f. → 3.1 (1).
  4. (3 marks) Distinguish elements, compounds and mixtures with one example each. Answer: element — one kind of atom, e.g. O₂ (1); compound — fixed ratio of elements, e.g. H₂O (1); mixture — variable composition, e.g. air (1).
  5. (3 marks) Readings of a 2.00 g mass: (i) 1.95, 1.93, 1.94 g; (ii) 2.01, 1.99, 2.00 g. Comment on accuracy and precision. Answer: (i) precise but not accurate (1); (ii) both precise and accurate (1); accuracy — closeness to 2.00; precision — closeness to each other (1).

Common mistakes

  1. Counting leading zeros. 2. Confusing accuracy and precision. 3. Mixture vs compound. 4. Litre conversions. 5. Rounding too early.

Quick recall

  1. 1 L in cm³? 2. SI unit of amount? 3. Air is? 4. 2.500 s.f.? 5. Precision means?

Answers: 1) 1000. 2) Mole. 3) Homogeneous mixture. 4) 4. 5) Closeness of repeated values.
